title: Optimal phase control of a measurement-assisted quantum refrigerator
summary: A tilted nonselective measurement can close the upper transition of a three-level quantum refrigerator, but it also generates coherence that feeds back on the populations and suppresses the cooling current. We formulate randomized open-loop control of the measurement azimuthal phase \(α\), sampled independently at each event from a probability distribution \(P(α)\), while keeping the event rate, polar angle, and single-event population-transfer probability fixed.
